r5_environment_prompts.forest:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: final environment art for a calm, physically scaled 2D microecosystem desktop application, landscape 16:9.
Input image 1 is the old R4 forest image: retain its natural pixel-art identity, green moss / warm decaying wood / grey stone palette, but REDESIGN the camera, object sizes and pixel fineness. Input image 2 is the user's moss-and-driftwood reference for intricately structured, deliberate small pixel clusters only. Do not copy its shrimp or exact composition.
Create an ENVIRONMENT ONLY, absolutely no animals, insects, snails or birds. No text, diagram, labels or UI.
Camera and scale: a low oblique near view across a real 45-centimeter-wide patch of damp woodland floor. This is a miniature patch of ordinary forest litter, not a landscape of giant logs or a distant forest clearing. Reference plane in the middle distance, fixed 16:9 composition. About 25–30cm depth front-to-back. A natural broken twig / small decaying branch about 24cm long and 3–4.5cm thick runs diagonally through the left middle third. No gigantic archway or theatrical cavern: just a narrow dark split beneath peeling bark, only about 1–2cm of headroom, appropriate for small woodlice. The supporting base, bark thickness, visible end grain and contact shadows must agree with this size.
Compose clear foreground, midground and background via overlapping real objects. Fallen serrated broadleaf leaves are about 4–6cm long, fine veins and curled thin edges; several leaves of different rotation and partial burial, never uniformly scattered decorative stamps. Main slate/rounded rocks 3–6cm across, grains and a few tiny pebbles 2–8mm. Moss mats 4–9cm wide with individual 4–9mm shoots and submillimeter leaflets; lush fine detailed moss, not giant fern-like moss branches. Two small fern crowns 8–12cm tall in back/side positions, with believable fine pinnae and delicate young growth, avoid fern leaves equal to wood thickness.
The central/lower middle retains visible moist earth and fine litter passages for future animals, with surfaces clearly distinguishable. On the left branch reserve a small fairly smooth dark bark patch; below it reserve a small accessible fissure entrance; at lower right a modest grey stone/leaf edge for scale anchors. Roots, fungi-like tiny growth and humus detail may be subtle. No unexplained glowing objects, huge mushrooms or giant grass.
Visual fineness: refined, densely crafted high-resolution PIXEL ART, small crisp square clusters and clean stepped contours, approximately a 960px-wide logical detail density across a 16:9 frame. Preserve deliberate pixel construction: NOT painterly blur, NOT smooth vector, NOT photographic rendering, NOT coarse 8-bit giant blocks. Texture follows bark fibres, leaf veins and moss shoots; material-specific detail, no uniform noise filter. Detailed enough for a large window while keeping large shapes readable at desktop-widget size.
Lighting: diffuse daylight with a small soft dappled patch, moderated yellow-green highlights, warm umber wood, deep cool green occlusion. High light does not outline every edge, no neon green carpet. Foreground edges partially frame the view, less saturated quieter background, dark voids only where geometry supports them. A cohesive natural-scale habitat photographed in spirit but painted entirely as pixel art.
Critical: do NOT reuse the old oversized woodlice/snail, remove all animal forms entirely. Increase fine environmental structure and visual realism of relative scale while retaining the accepted pixel style.
r5_environment_prompts.pond:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: environment-only pixel-art shallow-pond habitat for a Windows microecosystem desktop application, landscape 16:9.
Input image 1 is the previous R4 pond: preserve the accepted appealing pixel-art identity and general mossy driftwood, teal water and warm sand palette, but completely recalibrate the object scale and refine pixel detail. Input image 2 is the user's fine moss/driftwood artwork: use its fine pixel clusters, dark negative spaces and natural overlapping growth as texture reference only, not its close-up shrimp size.
Absolutely NO animals, shrimp, snails, fish, waterfleas or insects in this clean environment plate. No text, borders, UI, labels or scientific diagram.
Physical observation: a coherent window into an approximately 60cm-wide patch of shallow freshwater habitat, viewed obliquely from near bed level, roughly 25–30cm water depth visible. It is not a majestic underwater landscape, cave or aquarium poster. Fix the middle depth plane and let foreground/back objects scale together consistently. A waterlogged branching piece of wood about 34–40cm long and only 3–5cm thick crosses the middle at a modest diagonal; its fork rests on stones, with real contact and a modest gap only 3–5cm high under it, never a huge arch. All wood thickness, stone scale, roots, leaves and plant stems must support a later 2cm shrimp being a small inhabitant.
Use natural varied layers: 3–6cm rounded stones with small 2–8mm pebbles; fine sand patches and silt between stones; a couple of decaying 4–6cm submerged leaves with slender veins. Aquatic moss attached in 4–8cm patches, tiny 3–8mm shoots, delicate leaflets. Fine stem plants ~10–18cm tall, clear thin stems and centimeter-scale whorls; slender ribbon leaves partially curl with water. A few 5–8cm floating leaves near the upper edge with very thin hanging roots; those leaves must not dwarf the entire scene or resemble giant tree canopies. Reserve natural small bare resting/contact patches on wood, lower stones and leaf edge for future animals.
Atmospheric space: the foreground rocks/moss partially occlude parts of the wood; the wood in turn occludes some rear plants, silhouettes and water volume. Not everything is on one front-facing stage. A pale sand corridor winds diagonally through the mid/lower center, a few tiny darker debris particles, water becomes slightly quieter and less contrasty with distance. Clear natural pond water, no fog wall.
Render refined, intricate PIXEL ART with small intentionally shaped square clusters, clean stepped outlines, about a 960px-wide logical detail density. Match the approved style but substantially finer than the old huge blocks. Materials have distinct structure: splintered wood grain, fine moss shoots, granular sand, translucent layered water, thin leaf veins. NOT photorealistic, not oil painting, not smooth vector, no blur-and-sharpen texture, no uniform random noise.
Lighting is broken gentle surface light and restrained localized caustic flecks, no solid theatrical sunray cones. Rich fresh moss greens, subdued teal shadows, warm natural sand; avoid every plant glowing neon lime. Quiet and believable natural visual experience.
Critical: same-world scale throughout, small driftwood thickness and sensible plant leaf size; absolutely no embedded animals.

Optional only a handful of very tiny pale springtail-like short marks around damp moss/earth at x=.39,y=.70: each about1.5mm, at most0.33% image width or4–6 output pixels. They must not have large visible caricature limbs and must not be sized up to match woodlice.

No ruler, text, annotation, UI, picture frame, magnified inset or labels. Keep environment invariant.

r5_final_refinement_prompts.fauna:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: magnified creature morphology study for a refined pixel-art microecosystem. This is a shape-study board, NOT a scientific size chart. No numbers, labels, rulers, UI, watermarks or text. A calm pale cool grey background, six separated studies in an orderly three-column by two-row arrangement. Landscape3:2 image, generous margins and space between subjects. All creatures are separate, complete silhouettes with no cut-off body. Fine deliberate pixel clusters, understated natural materials, crisp stepped edges, refined pixel-art comparable to the tiny animals in the reference forest and pond habitat; NOT thick cartoon outlines, NO huge shiny eyes, no photographic cutout blur, no 3D render.
Top left: a grey common rounded woodlouse, natural dorsal three-quarter view, small head, modest antennae, seven overlapping trunk plates, many short ventral legs visibly supporting its body; no giant mammal face. Top middle: an elongate pale springtail, correctly a six-legged hexapod with long slender segmented antennae, soft slender abdomen and folded spring organ underneath; do not draw it as a miniature woodlouse or many-legged centipede. Top right: a SMALL woodland disc-snail morphology inspired by a6mm shell, low flattened brown disc-like ribbed coil, blue-grey slender extended body and two longer terrestrial eye tentacles plus smaller lower pair; the shell is much flatter and lower than a large garden snail, no giant glossy golden ball.
Bottom left: delicate freshwater dwarf shrimp, muted red with limited cream markings, articulated abdomen tapering to tail fan, small rostrum and dark eyes, fine long antennae and slender walking legs; specific scientific species is not claimed from color. Bottom middle: a translucent Daphnia-like waterflea, laterally compressed oval carapace, one small dark eye and branching swimming antennae, restrained internal hints, no cartoon face, no segmented shrimp-like tail. Bottom right: SMALL freshwater ramshorn snail morphology, flat coiled amber-brown shell viewed three-quarter side, narrow brown/grey foot and two thin non-eyestalk aquatic tentacles; visually distinct from the land snail at top right.
These are independently magnified morphology studies. Do not imitate an equal-actual-size population. Keep the microscopic springtail and waterflea studies visually a little smaller within their cells; exact physical sizes will be provided by a separately coded comparison chart. Target biological leg/antenna arrangement and physically grounded silhouette. No scenery or props; no contact shadow cast onto neighboring cells; faint minimal local grounding only.
